studies.title: Sworn By The Pen
studies.meaning: An oath by the pen and by what is written opens a defence, which is the point: the charge being answered is that the man speaking is mad, and the answer is sworn on writing. Three statements follow, each stronger than the last. He is not mad; his reward will not be cut off; and his character is described with a word for something vast. The last line simply says both sides will see.
studies.historicalContext: Meccan, and generally placed very early in the mission, among the first surahs after the opening revelation. The accusation of madness is reported in several sources as one of the labels the Meccan leadership settled on for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The surah answers it directly and at once, which is unusual: most Meccan surahs argue about God rather than about the messenger.

keyTerms.note: A reed cut to a point, the ordinary writing tool of the region. Swearing by it in a society that transmitted almost everything by memory gives writing a status the audience had not assigned it.
From a root meaning both to sever and to remind someone of a favour. A reward that is not of this kind is neither interrupted nor held over the recipient's head.
The first word names the settled disposition a person acts from, distinguished in Arabic from outward form by a single vowel. The second is the word used of the Throne and of the Day of Judgement.

studies.lifeInProphetsTime: Mecca ran on the spoken word. Contracts, genealogies and poetry were held in memory, and writing was a clerk's tool used for letters and accounts rather than a mark of prestige. Very few people wrote. An oath sworn by the pen would have sounded slightly odd to that audience, in the way an oath sworn by a filing cabinet would sound now.
studies.didYouKnow: Asked what the Prophet's character was like, one of his wives is reported to have answered in three words: it was the Quran. The report is among the most quoted in the tradition, and it takes the word used in this ayah and makes it a description of a text rather than of a temperament.
studies.theologicalSignificance: The defence offered is not a miracle and not an argument. It is a character reference, which locates the evidence for the message in the observable conduct of the person delivering it. That places a heavy weight on behaviour: if a life is the proof, then the proof is checkable by anyone who lives near it. The oath by writing at the head of the passage does something similar, staking the case on what can be recorded and revisited.

crossReferences.why: Names the pen again at the very beginning of the revelation, as the instrument of teaching.
Turns the character praised here into something a community is asked to look at and copy.
Answers the same accusation in another early surah, using the word companion to appeal to long acquaintance.

studies.applyIt: Think about what someone who has worked beside you for five years would say if asked what you are like. Not what you would want them to say. Then pick the one thing in that answer you would most like to change and choose a single occasion this week where you will handle it differently.
